items.title: Wilson "Chembo" Corniel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, November 15, 2019
items.q: we have a piano teacher here who played with Don Alias and he used to say that Don would have to like shave his calluses.

ctx.x: It doesn’t matter. Right. They have nothing to prove because they did what they had to do. But the thing is for him to be there and just to put the horn and get a sound out and still have the same melodic — you know he’s talking to you like he would speak to you. He’s not going to scream at you now, he’s not fifty years younger. You know I mean that’s how I see it, like you know music, it’ll never get old in you because it’s part of you. It’s part of your vocal.

Is there any physicality — I mean I know there’s physicality to what you do. Does it manifest itself, like do you get sore? Like I remember this anecdote, we have a piano teacher here who played with Don Alias and he used to say that Don would have to like shave his calluses.

Yeah. Well it depends on your hands too. You know each one — my hand sweats a little bit so there’s a little moisture, you know drier hands, you know so it depends some it all plays a factor. This winter weather here chaps up my hands, cracks my hands a lot. I’m
